title: On the Performance and Scalability of Cloud Supercomputers: Insights from Eagle and Reindeer
problem: Cloud-based supercomputers (Azure Eagle, Reindeer) represent new HPC models, but their performance and scalability characteristics remain poorly understood. Misconceptions exist about virtualization overhead and cloud performance vs. bare-metal systems.
motivation: Cloud platforms are expanding HPC capabilities, but lack of public performance data prevents informed adoption decisions. Need for systematic comparison of cloud and bare-metal systems to understand cloud viability for HPC workloads.
method: Comparative analysis of two Azure cloud supercomputers: Eagle (ranked 3 on Top500, 14,400 H100 GPUs) and Reindeer (ranked 32 on Top500, 960 H200 GPUs). Uses microbenchmarks, synthetic workloads, and scientific workflows including HPL. Evaluates computational efficiency, scaling, communication bandwidth, network latency, and virtualization overhead. Compares against bare-metal on-premises systems.
key_novelty: First systematic performance comparison of cloud-based supercomputers against bare-metal systems; quantifies virtualization overhead impact; demonstrates competitive cloud HPC performance.
contributions: Comparative performance analysis of Azure Eagle and Reindeer
Scaling efficiency assessment (86% weak scaling for Eagle)

metrics.communication: Comparable to bare-metal latencies, better throughput

limitations: Applicability to data-intensive workloads not discussed
Comparison to non-cloud GPU systems (Frontier, Perlmutter) limited
Long-term stability and reliability over extended runs not discussed
